Plot time to an event

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotSurvival.R, R/zzz-mae.R
plotSurvival.Rd

plotSurvival() draws Kaplan-Meier curves of the time from each subject's first sample to an event: dropout, the arrival or loss of a feature, leaving the first state, or a clinical outcome.

Usage

plotSurvival(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotSurvival(
  x,
  time.col,
  group,
  event = c("dropout", "arrival", "loss", "state.exit", "outcome"),
  group.by = NULL,
  feature = NULL,
  assay.type = "counts",
  detection = 0,
  state.col = NULL,
  event.col = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotSurvival(x, ..., experiment = 1L)

Arguments

x

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

additional arguments passed to geom_step.

time.col

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that contains sampling times: numeric, Date, POSIXct or a factor of visits.

group

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that identifies subjects.

event

Character scalar. The event: the last sample of a subject is before the latest sampling time in x ("dropout"); feature is present after being absent at the first sample ("arrival") or absent after being present ("loss"); state.col differs from the first sample ("state.exit"); or event.col is TRUE ("outcome"). (Default: "dropout")

group.by

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that splits the subjects into curves, taken from their first sample. (Default: NULL)

feature

Character scalar. Specifies the feature for event = "arrival" and "loss". A feature is present when its value in assay.type is above detection. (Default: NULL)

assay.type

Character scalar. Specifies the assay for feature. (Default: "counts")

detection

Numeric scalar. Specifies the value above which feature is present. (Default: 0)

state.col

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) with the state of each sample, for event = "state.exit". (Default: NULL)

event.col

Character scalar. Specifies the logical column from colData(x) that marks the samples where the outcome has occurred, for event = "outcome". (Default: NULL)

experiment

Character scalar or integer scalar. For a MultiAssayExperiment, the experiment to plot; its samples get the colData of x. (Default: 1L)

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Follow-up starts at the first sample of each subject. A subject without the event is censored at its last sample, marked with a cross. The band is the 95\ are only seen at sampling times, so the event time is the first sample at which the event is observed, an upper bound of the true time.

A subject drops out when its last sample precedes the last sampling time of the study, the latest time in x. A subject that joins late and is sampled until the end is not a dropout. For "arrival" and "loss", only subjects without and with the feature at their first sample are at risk. Times are in time.col units: days for Date, hours for POSIXct times and visit steps for visits.

References

Kaplan EL, Meier P (1958). Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. Journal of the American Statistical Association 53(282):457-481.

Examples

# Time until the dominant genus changes, by sex
data("hitchip1006", package = "miaTime")
tse <- mia::addDominant(hitchip1006, name = "dominant")
tse <- tse[, tse$subject %in% names(which(table(tse$subject) >= 2))]
plotSurvival(tse, time.col = "time", group = "subject",
    event = "state.exit", state.col = "dominant", group.by = "sex")
